response: Yes, Web-based and clinic samples of gay men living with HIV do differ on self-reported physical and psychological symptoms. Compared to the clinic sample, the Web-based sample had a worse psychological symptom burden. Additionally, the Web-based sample tended to be younger, have a higher prevalence of employment, and a lower proportion on antiretroviral therapy (ART). These differences highlight the importance of considering demographic variables and potential sampling biases when collecting data from different sources, such as Web-based surveys and clinic samples.
